sections.h2: Why does Jasper County, Georgia feel so rural?
sections.html:
Scale is small in every direction. Only one city exists, Monticello, which doubles as the county seat; the one town is Shady Dale; and the 2020 count listed the whole population as rural. Area comes to 373 square miles, with roughly 5 of that water.

Legislators created the county on December 10, 1807 out of Baldwin County territory under the name Randolph; the switch to Sergeant William Jasper's name came in 1812, per Wikipedia. Newton County later took a piece of its land, in 1821.

Morgan, Putnam, Jones, Monroe, Butts and Newton counties surround it. Federal land claims part of the map, since portions of the Oconee National Forest and the Piedmont National Wildlife Refuge lie within its borders. Runoff west of State Route 11 reaches the Upper Ocmulgee, and the eastern half feeds the Upper Oconee. Public education is a four-school system that includes Jasper County High School.

sections.h2: How is the Jasper County housing market shaped?
sections.html:
Think small, owner-heavy and speeding up. Mid-2025 estimates give Jasper County 17,632 residents, up 20.8% against the 2020 starting point, where the prior decade added only 4.9%.

The 1970 census found only 5,760 residents. Atlanta's metro area reaches into the county, according to Wikipedia, and an average trip to work of nearly 40 minutes reflects that. Of 6,270 housing units in 2020, 13.7% stood vacant, and there were 39.6 residents for each square mile. Anyone buying acreage is likely to raise questions on wells, septic and frontage.

QuickFacts counts 5,965 households averaging 2.65 people. Few move: 91.8% of residents were in the same home a year earlier. Minors are 22.6% of the population and seniors 19.2%.

High school graduates make up 89.6% of adults, and 19.5% went on to a bachelor's degree. Monthly owner costs are $1,461 with a mortgage and $480 without. Employers numbered 225 in 2023, with 1,911 employees, and 13.2% of residents fall below the poverty line.

Those carrying costs help when you test an asking price against the $243,400 middle value.

sections.h2: Which office answers which Jasper County tax question?
sections.html:
A bill passes through several hands, and the Tax Commissioner's are the last. Millage comes from the commission and school board, value from the assessors, dispute rulings from a board the Grand Jury appoints, and mailing and collecting from the commissioner.

  • Tax Commissioner: 126 W. Greene Street, Suite 125, Monticello, GA 31064; (706) 468-4902; counter open Monday through Friday, 8 to 4:30
  • Tax Assessor: signs off on exemptions and notifies owners when it changes a value
  • Clerk of Superior Court: the courthouse deed room provides warranty deed copies

One mill is a dollar per thousand of assessed value, and 40% of market value is the assessed figure.

sections.h2: When does a Jasper County bill come due?
sections.html:
On the standing schedule, land, buildings and business personal property are paid in two halves, September 20 and December 20. The state's county facts sheet names December 20 as the default statewide due date and gives every taxpayer 60 days from the postmark before interest begins.

The 2026 notice departed from that schedule: mailing on October 16, a first installment dated November 20, and the balance dated December 20. Dates have shifted from year to year, so trust the ones on your own bill.

  • Manufactured housing: payment and a location permit by April 1 each year
  • Missing it brings a 10% penalty and possibly a citation to Magistrate Court or sale of the unit
  • Vehicles renew during the 30 days that end on the owner's birthday

sections.h2: How can unpaid Jasper County tax affect a sale?
sections.html:
Liens tend to appear when a sale is about to close. Taxes left unpaid past 90 days are recorded as a tax FiFa with the Clerk of Superior Court, and the county warns that property can be levied on and sold.

Anyone can read a FiFa entry, bureaus included, and the tax office says it cannot dictate how they use it. Clear a recorded lien before closing.

The balance is available at (706) 468-4902. If your closing falls between the two installment dates, settle who pays each half and put that in the settlement papers.

sections.h2: What exemptions does Jasper County list?
sections.html:
The base exemption is two thousand dollars off assessed value. It reduces the county, school and State levies, but the share of the rate that retires bonds is excluded.

  • Owners 62 and over (school tax): as much as ten thousand dollars off, for net income not above that same figure, and bond levies are covered
  • Owners 65 and over (general): as much as four thousand dollars for an applicant and spouse earning ten thousand or less, with Social Security and certain retirement income set aside
  • Veterans with service-connected disabilities: $63,780 at most; a surviving spouse who has not remarried gets the same if the service member died in armed conflict
  • Owners 65 and over (State levy): the whole value of the house and as many as 10 acres, if you qualify under another homestead category

Bring a driver's license showing your Jasper County address when you apply at the Tax Commissioner. A form received by April 1 counts for that year. Approval carries over each year until you move, change owners or switch type, and a bigger local exemption replaces the State figure.

sections.h2: How do I dispute a Jasper County value?
sections.html:
The clock is 45 days from the notice date. Your choices are the Board of Equalization or an arbitrator, and a written notice to the Board of Tax Assessors sends either result up to Superior Court.

Preparation helps. During the January 1 to April 1 return period an owner can state a personal view of market value, which creates solid ground if the assessors alter it. Mobile home owners have 45 days to file with the assessors and 21 days after a change notice to reach the Board of Equalization.

sections.h2: Can Jasper County tax be refunded, and who bills city tax?
sections.html:
Yes, within limits. A written request can recover tax assessed or collected in error or illegally, started within three years of paying. When the claim comes from an appealed value, the refund is processed once the final taxable value is fixed.

City tax is a separate levy. Municipalities tax on their own, and the city clerk sends and collects that bill unless city and county have agreed on one combined bill. Vehicle tax is always collected by the county Tax Commissioner.

Holders of long-term notes secured by real estate must record them within 90 days, at the state's intangible recording rate of $1.50 per $500 of face amount or part of it.

sections.h2: What do returns and special programs involve in Jasper County?
sections.html:
Returns for taxable property are accepted January 1 through April 1. An owner who files none is treated as repeating last year's value and last year's real property exemptions.

Mail goes to the last address the county has, so report any move. Three programs change how land or buildings are valued.

  • Historic property: a building on the Georgia register, with up to two acres around it, may be assessed preferentially
  • Brownfield sites: land approved for cleanup can keep a frozen value for a decade
  • Public safety survivors: the unremarried spouse of a firefighter or officer killed on duty may be fully exempt once the agency's papers are filed

If your property is in a program, the Board of Tax Assessors can say what a buyer must do to keep the status.

faqs.q: What is the street address for the Jasper County tax counter?
faqs.a: 126 W. Greene Street, Suite 125, Monticello, GA 31064, telephone (706) 468-4902. Weekday hours run 8 to 4:30.

faqs.q: Deadline for a first Jasper County homestead claim?
faqs.a: April 1 of the first year. Anything later counts toward the next tax year, and the home must have been yours and lived in on January 1.

faqs.q: Does a Jasper County tax lien reach my credit file?
faqs.a: Possibly. Ninety days past due puts a FiFa lien on record with the Clerk of Superior Court, and those entries are public.

faqs.q: How do I get a Jasper County deed copy?
faqs.a: Visit the deed room of the Clerk of Superior Court in the Jasper County Courthouse.

faqs.q: What is the Jasper County appeal deadline?
faqs.a: Forty-five days from the date printed on the assessment notice. A later written notice to the Board of Tax Assessors carries a ruling to Superior Court.
